entities.name: PMID:25445244
observations: 2015 Journal of Neuroscience Methods paper on comprehensive EEG/ERP analysis in the ADHD go/no-go paradigm.
The abstract reports two spatiotemporally distinct processes, one possibly attention-related and one more perception-related.
The authors suggest averaged EEG/ERP signals may reduce to a parsimonious set of underlying neurophysiological processes.
The available abstract does not provide named components, numerical group effects, or time-frequency results.

entities.name: PMID:23805094
observations: Related 2013 Frontiers in Human Neuroscience methodological paper using spatiotemporal segregation in the go/no-go task.
The abstract states that theory-based EEG markers can differentiate normal and ADHD subjects and that modeled processes may belong to a limited reusable set.

entities.name: Parsimonious EEG processes
observations: In the ADHD go/no-go paradigm, comprehensive assumption-light analysis identified two spatiotemporally distinct processes broadly related to attention and perception.
This supports a qualified parsimonious-process interpretation of averaged EEG/ERP signals, but not universal simplicity or a single unitary ADHD mechanism.
